claims.claim: García says the section on Robert's Rebellion is limited and particular because Yandel is aware he must be careful writing about very powerful people like Tywin Lannister.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)

claims.claim: García says they invented a great many books and maesters for the text to cite, which was the one area where Martin let them have fun.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: A lot of books we came up with
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: García says his favourite passages from Martin are very poetic passages and names the first Areo Hotah chapter, calling the prose gorgeous.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)

claims.claim: García says Martin is fantastic at creating atmosphere and theme while Guy Gavriel Kay is almost poetic in how he writes, a distinctly different manner.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: George is fantastic in creating atmosphere and theme

claims.claim: Antonsson says they cut Martin's originally written material down to fit The World of Ice and Fire, and that the unedited material later went into Fire & Blood.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: we started cutting the material down to fit into this book

claims.claim: García says version control between Martin's original WordStar files and the edited documents was a problem, because Martin often worked from files that had not been through Groell's editing.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr. and Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: the all versioning control was definitely a bit of a problem

claims.claim: Antonsson says they helped Anne Groell go over the Fire & Blood material and try to keep it consistent with The World of Ice and Fire.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: try and keep it consistent between the two books

claims.claim: Groell says elements of The World of Ice and Fire had to be shortened because the book was already getting too long.
claims.source: Anne Groell, Suvudu Universe Q&A re-transcribed at The Fireside (2014-05-29)
claims.quote: mainly because we had to shorten a
claims.page: Q&A, answer on knowing the ending

claims.claim: Groell says Martin had to reveal a few secrets to her so that she could help him redirect parts of the plot of The World of Ice and Fire.
claims.source: Anne Groell, Suvudu Universe Q&A re-transcribed at The Fireside (2014-05-29)
claims.quote: to reveal a few secrets so I could help him redirect parts of the plot
claims.page: Q&A, answer on knowing the ending

claims.claim: Groell says seven books is what is currently under contract and recounts answering each of Martin's revised estimates with Seven Books for Seven Kingdoms.
claims.source: Anne Groell, Suvudu Universe Q&A re-transcribed at The Fireside (2014-05-29)

claims.claim: Martin says internal consistency is a good objective yardstick by which to judge a piece of fiction.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, "Critics and Reviewers", GoH speech, Othercon III (1979-09-29)
claims.quote: internal consistency is to my mind a good objective yardstick
claims.page: speech, disclaimers before the three rules

claims.claim: Martin says the ideal reader is absorbed into the narrative and lives events as the viewpoint character lives them, learning things as he learns them.
claims.quote: lives events as the viewpoint character lives them
claims.page: speech, section on the vicarious experience

claims.claim: Martin says that when he writes a story he organises events and information as carefully as he can to give the reader a vicarious experience.
claims.quote: I organize things — events and information and the like
claims.page: speech, section on the vicarious experience

claims.claim: Martin says we read fiction to find out what happens.
claims.quote: We read fiction to find out what happens

claims.claim: Martin says the ending of a piece of fiction should grow out of what has gone before and be logical, consistent and integral to the rest of the story.
claims.quote: it needs to be logical and consistent and integral
claims.page: speech, section on the protected ending
